verifiedRecords.graph: Undirected simple graph with n known labeled vertices, m edges and maximum degree Δ
verifiedRecords.output: One explicit color assignment for every edge
verifiedRecords.oracle: degree(v) and indexed neighbor(v,i); arbitrary local list order
verifiedRecords.queryComplexity: Exactly n+2m oracle calls for this scan
verifiedRecords.queryDerivation: Ask degree(v) once for each of n vertices; then read all degree(v) list entries. The sum of degrees is 2m. Retain each undirected edge once and make no further external graph queries.
verifiedRecords.totalTimeConvention: Total RAM time includes the O(n+m) scan and the post-scan computation shown separately.
verifiedRecords.memory: Stores the full O(n+m)-word adjacency representation; no auxiliary-space restriction imposed.
verifiedRecords.bound: Exactly n+2m oracle calls for this scan; O(mΔ) post-scan time
verifiedRecords.guarantee: Proper coloring using at most 2Δ−1 colors
verifiedRecords.sourceLocation: Greedy palette observation in Introduction; straightforward RAM implementation is an atlas derivation
verifiedRecords.notes: Each edge has at most 2Δ−2 colored neighbors; scanning these and the 2Δ−1 palette costs O(Δ) per edge. The oracle scan is an atlas composition. The same O(mΔ) greedy bound is explicitly discussed in Bernshteyn–Dhawan §1.1/Table 1.
verifiedRecords.quality: Proper coloring using at most 2Δ−1 colors
verifiedRecords.theorem: Greedy palette observation in Introduction; straightforward RAM implementation is an atlas derivation
assumptions: Δ≥1; empty graphs handled trivially
Scan neighboring edge colors and choose a free color for each edge
This is a straightforward greedy implementation, not an optimal implementation of greedy coloring

A unit-cost operation emits O(1) assignments

derivedBounds.proof: The requested output has m records. If one operation emits at most a constant number of records, emitting the output takes at least a constant multiple of m operations, even if the graph and coloring are already known.
derivedBounds.theorem: Elementary output-counting derivation by the atlas; not a paper theorem
derivedBounds.notes: This is a time lower bound only. It is not a degree/neighbor-query lower bound, a palette lower bound, or a query-optimality claim.
